scope: Seven additional pinned text/specification/config/fixture files read whole and Git blob matched. Configured shell commands treated as data, not executed.

findings.detail: ECC example specifies marker-delimited entries with relative path, size, metadata ECC and repeated per-block hash/ECC. It is illustrative and does not itself specify marker escaping, authoritative whole-file content identity, or parsing resource bounds.

Easy scenario actively generates and repairs header ECC only; whole-file adaptive ECC lines are commented. Hard scenario comments out generation/repair and actively injects noise. Their names do not establish broad repair coverage.

Configs request probabilistic noise and bursts without explicit random seed or expected byte-change manifest. Reproducibility and measured corruption counts require runtime recording, not config presence.

Three small tracked text fixtures are available and now read; original PDF/JPEG/ZIP fixtures remain unreviewed and absent from this local cache. Reading these text files does not qualify image/container repair tests.
